clue.text: I've locks unkempt and in a sad state

indicators.note: unkempt hair is untidy and out of order, so the letters beside it are to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits their hair is a mess and they are miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unkempt' is the anagram signal for the letters of I'VE LOCKS; 'and' merely joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym by description: a person pining with unrequited passion is miserable and languishing.

clue.text: Porcelain container: briefly hurried to fill it

indicators.note: the hurried word goes inside the container, 'it' pointing back to that container

parts.note: a jar is a container for jam or pickles

indicators.note: briefly asks for the word to be cut short by its final letter

parts.note: sped is the past tense of speed, meaning hurried

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to top up a china pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens the hurried word and 'to fill it' sends the result inside the container. 'Porcelain' is the definition: Wedgwood, the English pottery firm, made a fine unglazed stoneware of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Wedgwood's fine matt stoneware of this name is loosely classed as a ceramic of the china kind.

clue.text: Turning tin opener to hand round a snack

indicators.note: turning asks for the word for tin to be read from back to front

parts.note: a tin and a can are the same metal food container

indicators.note: the opener to a word is the letter that starts it

parts.note: the letter O is a round shape

explanation.surface: Someone twists a can opener and passes a nibble around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reads the tin backwards, 'opener to' takes the start of hand, and 'round' is a letter by its shape. The surface's tin opener is split across two devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tortilla chip topped with melted cheese is a popular nibble.

clue.text: Take a gamble embracing men in a strange garden

indicators.note: in places the first group of letters inside the phrase that follows it

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: embracing means the gamble wraps its arms round the men

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A warning about risking money while hugging blokes in an odd park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' and 'in' nest three layers. 'Take' is no instruction here: on old prescriptions the Latin recipe, meaning take, was abbreviated to one letter. The first 'a' is padding; the second is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a botanical collection of trees is one kind of planted ground open to visitors.

clue.text: Game father embraces precocious girl, losing head

indicators.note: embraces means the father word wraps round the girl's name

parts.note: to sire is to father offspring

indicators.note: losing head removes the first letter of the girl's name

parts.note: Lolita is the precocious girl of Nabokov's novel

explanation.surface: A dad hugs a forward young lass who is panicking during some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' beheads the title girl of Nabokov's novel before 'embraces' wraps the father round her. The surface's embrace is unsettlingly close to the novel's plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a card pastime for one player, also called patience in Britain.

clue.text: Advantages with European plain speaking

parts.note: pros are the advantages in 'pros and cons'

explanation.surface: The benefits of talking bluntly with someone from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: ordinary language without metre or rhyme is the unadorned way of talking and writing.

clue.text: Like the Raj with no end in India would be put at risk

indicators.note: with no means the letter named next is taken away

parts.note: the Raj was British rule in India, so it was imperial

indicators.note: the end in a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: British rule in India, seemingly endless, would face danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end in' picks the A of India and 'with no' removes it from IMPERIAL. The Raj was the period of British rule over India.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to endanger something is to expose it to danger.

clue.text: Superficial glamour can mostly be bought

parts.note: a tin is the British word for a can

indicators.note: mostly keeps all of the word but its final letter

parts.note: goods that sell are goods that get bought

explanation.surface: Showy glitz is usually something money can buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' shortens only the word for 'be bought', in the sense that goods which are bought are goods that move off the shelf. 'can' looks like a verb but is the metal container.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: the glittering Christmas decoration stands for showy but shallow attraction.

clue.text: Call for concert piano tuner's head

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms held each summer in London
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A request goes out for the top man who tunes the recital's keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes the T of tuner's. A prom is a British promenade concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to elicit or give rise to something, as a remark may elicit a reply.

clue.text: Take tea around motorway somewhere in central Europe

indicators.note: around puts the tea word round the motorway

parts.note: bohea is a black China tea
the M1 is a British motorway, its figure 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Stopping for a cuppa near a main road on a continental trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps an old name for black China tea round Britain's first motorway, its digit read as a letter. 'Take' is just the instruction to the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the historic western region of the Czech lands lies in the middle of the continent.

clue.text: Swamp obscuring small lake in Ireland

indicators.note: obscuring means the letter that follows is hidden from view, so dropped

parts.note: a slough is a swamp or bog
S is the clothing-label abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A bog hides a little stretch of water in the Irish countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscuring' removes the S from SLOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: it is the Irish word for a body of inland water, as in Neagh.

clue.text: Something like me before church, say

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the church letters

parts.note: 'me' is an example of a pronoun
CE is the abbreviation for Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone resembling the speaker stands in front of a chapel, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' gives the order. 'say' looks like the usual for-example marker but is the definition; 'me' is the word itself, not the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to utter or articulate words.

clue.text: Go down with workers beginning on the river basin

parts.note: to go down with flu is to catch it
men is a common word for a workforce

indicators.note: the beginning on a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A descent with labourers starting work in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning on' takes the T of the. 'Go down with' is illness, not descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the area of land draining into one watercourse.

clue.text: What keeps fire in when Bonfire night is begun on the fourth?

indicators.note: the month is started from its fourth letter, so its first three letters go

parts.note: Bonfire Night, Britain's Guy Fawkes celebration, falls on 5 November
the three letters ahead of the fourth, which are passed over

explanation.surface: A puzzle about keeping a blaze alight if the celebration started a day early.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonfire Night is 5 November in Britain; 'begun on the fourth' starts NOVEMBER at its fourth letter, dropping NOV. The fourth sounds like the date.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a glowing coal in the ashes holds the heat from which flames can be revived.

clue.text: Pickpocket mostly besets English in ferry port

indicators.note: besets means the thief surrounds the English letter
mostly keeps all of the word except its final letter

parts.note: dipper is slang for a pickpocket, one who dips into pockets

explanation.surface: A thief generally preys on British travellers at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts DIPPER to DIPPE and 'besets' wraps it round E. The town is the French end of the Channel crossing from Newhaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Normandy harbour town is a terminal for cross-Channel boats.

clue.text: Where there may be stained glass with varied patterns

definitions.text: Where there may be stained glass

indicators.note: varied means changed, so the letters of the next word are changed about

explanation.surface: A place with coloured windows in assorted designs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' signals the anagram of PATTERNS; 'with' joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the cross-arm of a church often has large coloured windows.

clue.text: Gets rudeness for rapid fall in real estate?

parts.note: to land a job is to get it
lip is slang for cheek or insolent talk

explanation.surface: Someone is abused as property prices crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a joke: earth sliding down a hillside is literally ground dropping fast, dressed up as a property crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: a mass of earth sliding downhill is ground itself dropping quickly.

clue.text: See pub's not large for singing performance

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see, used in references

indicators.note: not means the letter for large is taken out of the pub word

parts.note: a local is British slang for the pub nearest your home
L is the clothing-label abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: The bar looks too small to host a music night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the first L from LOCAL, a Briton's neighbourhood pub. V for 'See' is Latin vide.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: the sung part of a recording, as in a lead track by the singer.

clue.text: Don't hold back a germinating rose plant

definitions.meaning: to speak or act bluntly and without hesitation
a fanciful description: a rose's fruit holds its seeds, so a seedling would be a sprout emerging out of that fruit

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to act or speak without restraint, and read literally it pictures a sprout emerging out of a rose's fruit.

clue.text: Like some conductors convince one with note length

parts.note: to coax is to persuade or talk someone round
the Roman numeral for one is I
A is a note of the musical scale
L is the abbreviation for length in measurements

explanation.surface: Certain orchestra leaders can win a player over by holding a tone.
explanation.walkthrough: The conductors are electrical cables, not people with batons.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: cables with a core and a surrounding sheath sharing one axis carry signals to televisions.

clue.text: Certainly no effect of global warming is very little

definitions.text: Certainly no effect of global warming
definitions.meaning: a playful literal reading: warming makes sea levels rise, so the sea falling is the last thing it would cause
the idiom for a tiny amount beside what is needed

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a negligible amount, and taken literally it pictures sea level falling, the opposite of what a hotter planet brings.

clue.text: Oil particular part on stripped-down pump

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the earlier pieces sit above the last one

parts.note: pet means special or particular, as in a pet hate
a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: stripped-down removes the outer letters of the word, leaving its inside

explanation.surface: A mechanic lubricates one component of a dismantled engine pump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped-down' leaves UM from pump, and 'on' stacks PET and ROLE above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: crude mineral fuel pumped out of the ground.

clue.text: Drinking glass for stranger

definitions.meaning: a large stemmed tumbler for wine or spirits
the comparative of the British slang adjective for odd

explanation.definitionFit: It names a large stemmed vessel for wine, and is also the comparative of a slang word for odd.

clue.text: Sailor transported is no longer here

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
something sent has been dispatched or conveyed

explanation.surface: A seaman shipped off to the colonies has gone away.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: away, missing from the place.

clue.text: Turn sanctimonious over casino game after losing pounds

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: pi is old British slang for pious or sanctimonious

indicators.note: after losing means the letter for pounds is dropped out of the game

parts.note: roulette is a casino game played with a wheel
L is the old abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A gambler becomes self-righteous about the tables once the money has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after losing' drops the pounds abbreviation out of the wheel game, and 'over' stacks the old slang for pious above it. 'Turn' reads as a verb but names the dancer's spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a ballet dancer's spin on one foot is a kind of rotation.

clue.text: Treat raw fragments to give creature on the river

indicators.note: fragments, as a verb, means breaks into pieces, so these letters break up and re-form

explanation.surface: Feeding uncooked scraps to an animal living by the stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fragments' is the anagram signal for TREAT RAW; 'to give' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the vole of that name, like Ratty in The Wind in the Willows, lives on stream banks.

clue.text: Cut the crown off cork hat

indicators.note: in a down clue the crown is the top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a cork is a stopper for a bottle
the top letter of the word for cork, which is cut away

explanation.surface: Someone trims the top from a piece of headgear made of bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut the crown off' removes the S that begins STOPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name: the tall formal silk headgear worn with morning dress.

clue.text: Reinforcing vaccine's first stage

definitions.meaning: a follow-up jab that renews immunity
the rocket section that fires at lift-off and then falls away

explanation.definitionFit: It names both a follow-up jab that tops up immunity and the part of a rocket that fires at lift-off.

clue.text: Still cold when wrapped in tartan cloth

indicators.note: wrapped in means the cold letter is enclosed by the cloth

parts.note: plaid is the chequered woollen cloth of Scottish dress
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone remains chilly despite being bundled in a Highland blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when wrapped in' puts C inside PLAID. 'Still' reads as an adverb but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: calm and unruffled, like motionless water.

clue.text: Half-heartedly steal gold coin

indicators.note: the word has a doubled letter at its heart, and half of that pair is dropped

parts.note: nobble is British slang for to steal or grab dishonestly
one of the two matching letters at the centre of the slang word

explanation.surface: A thief pockets a sovereign without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' drops one of the two Bs in the middle of NOBBLE, British slang for swiping.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an old English piece of money struck in that precious metal, worth a third of a pound.
